props.title: Fallen

sections.content: Fallen masterfully blends supernatural horror with detective noir, following Denzel Washington as Detective John Hobbes hunting a serial killer who can transfer his consciousness between bodies through touch. The film's ingenious use of "Time Is On My Side" creates unbearable tension, similar to how The Exorcist (1973) forever changed "Tubular Bells." This demonic possession thriller shares DNA with Angel Heart (1987) and The First Power (1990) in mixing police procedural with supernatural horror, but adds the unique terror of a demon who can instantly possess anyone.

sections.content: The film's brilliant opening sequence sets up its unreliable narrator framework, much like The Usual Suspects (1995), but with a supernatural twist. Director Gregory Hoblit, who mastered crime thrillers with Primal Fear (1996), brings a gritty authenticity to the supernatural elements. The possession mechanics - requiring touch and signaled by visible breath in any temperature - created a new mythology that influenced later films like Fallen Angels (2006) and Incarnate (2016).

John Goodman and Donald Sutherland deliver stellar supporting performances that ground the supernatural elements in believable police work. The film's exploration of ancient Aramaic and theological horror draws from The Seventh Sign (1988) and The Prophecy (1995), while its theme of an unstoppable supernatural force pursuing its victim influenced It Follows (2014). sections.content: Fallen's influence can be seen in later supernatural detective films like Constantine (2005) and Deliver Us from Evil (2014), which similarly blend police work with demonic threats. The film's approach to possession - making anyone a potential threat - created a template for paranoid supernatural thrillers like The Hidden (1987) and modern works like The Empty Man (2020).
